sentences.text: Shanweiniao is a member of the class Aves, specifically within the subclass Enantiornithes. It belongs to the family Longipterygidae, a group of long-beaked enantiornithean birds that also includes Longipteryx, Longirostravis, and Rapaxavis.

Only a single fossil specimen, consisting of a slab and counterslab, is known for Shanweiniao. The fossil was collected from the Dawangzhengzi Beds of the middle Yixian Formation in Lingyuan, Liaoning Province, China. It is now housed at the Dalian Natural History Museum with accession numbers DNHM D1878/1 and DNHM1878/2.
The species name cooperorum honors Carl and Lynn Cooper for funding the study of Mesozoic birds in China.
Although originally thought to be arboreal, Shanweiniao appears to have been terrestrial, similar to megapodes and larks.
This animal lived between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago, spanning the Barremian to Aptian stages.
Researchers later stated that interpretations of Shanweiniao's tail morphology are speculative because the feathers of the holotype are incompletely preserved.
